findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
The following surfaces were observed to be in need of cleaning:

1. The fan vent in the reach-in cooler by the handwashing sink was observed to have soil accumulation.
2. The outer surface of the juice machine, especially the surface close to the orange juice nozzle was observed to have soil accumulation.
3. The reach-in freezer between the reach-in cooler and Avantco reach-in freezer was observed to have ice build up on the wall surface.

The person-in-charge was instructed to have those surfaces cleaned by the inspector. Ensure the non-food contact surfaces are kept free of ice buildup and soil accumulation.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(B) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. [C]

findings.title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
findings.comment: No ambient thermometers were observed in the standing cooler by the handwashing sink and milk cooler. The person-in-charge (PIC) was informed and instructed to provide internal thermometers in each cooler to allow for proper temperature monitoring, especially in the event of equipment failure. Ensure ambient thermometers are placed in the warmest part of each cooler to accurately monitor internal temperatures.
findings.citation_text: 4-204.112(A) Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) In a mechanically refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, the sensor of a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure the air temperature or a simulated product temperature in the warmest part of a mechanically refrigerated unit and in the coolest part of a hot FOOD storage unit. [C]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:

1. The fan vent in the standing cooler by the handwashing sink was observed to have soil accumulation.
2. The inner top surface above the coffee filter was observed to have soil accumulation.
3. The outer surface of the juice machine, especially the surface close to the orange juice nozzle was observed to have soil accumulation.

The PIC was instructed to have those surfaces cleaned by the inspector. Ensure non-food contact surfaces are kept free of soil accumulation.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(B) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Inspector observed dirty mop water and mop head being stored in the mop bucket in the back room of the storage area. Discussed with PIC and the wastewater was disposed properly and the mop head stored properly. Ensure that dirty mop water is disposed properly and mop heads be stored in a way that allow it to air dry.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.15 Cleaning Maintenance Tools, Preventing Contamination. FOOD preparation sinks, HANDWASHING SINKS, and WAREWASHING EQUIPMENT may not be used for the cleaning of maintenance tools, the preparation or holding of maintenance materials, or the disposal of mop water and similar liquid wastes.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the floor base cove pulling away from the wall in the area left of the dish machine and the space between the three compartment sink and the refrigeration units. Ensure that the necessary repaire are done sealing the above mentioned areas.
findings.citation_text: 6-201.13(A) Floor and Wall Junctures, Coved, and Enclosed or Sealed. (A) In FOOD ESTABLISHMENTS in which cleaning methods other than water flushing are used for cleaning floors, the floor and wall junctures shall be coved and closed to no larger than 1 mm (one thirty-second inch).

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-201.13: Observed floor base cove is pulling away from the wall in the area left of the dish machine. Repair or replace this cove piece. 

(A) floor and wall junctures shall be coved and closed to no larger than 1mm (one thirty-second inch). (B) Floors in which water flush cleaning methods are used shall be provided with drains and be graded to drain. Floor and wall junctures shall be coved and SEALED.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Inspector observed the dish machine to be operating at 0ppm of chlorine sanitizer. The line to the sanitizer bottle was adjusted, sanitizer primed, and the machine tested at 50ppm of chlorine. The 50ppm is consistent with the machine data plate requirements.  The violation is considered corrected on site. Take care to verify sanitizer concentration with test strips daily in both types of sanitizer used in the facility. 

4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
findings.comment:
2-501.11: A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. Reference 2-501.11.  

Observed no Norovirus illness clean-up policy at the facility. Facility has had a change in management since last inspection. Current CFPM/GM did not have previous paperwork. Provided copy of the Norovirus illness clean-up policy. Facility has bleach to perform procedure. No bodily fluid clean-up kit on hand. Discussed that if facility chooses, call EcoLab and they can provide a bodily fluid clean-up kit that will kill for Norovirus. COS.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. 

Observed no paper towels at the paper towel dispenser next to the hand sink in the kitchen. Discussed with employee and CFPM/GM. Employee went to back to obtain paper towels. Employee was using reusable sani bucket rags to dry hands (clean rags). Ensure disposable paper towels remain at the hand sink during all hours of operation. COS.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. 

(REPEAT) Observed no CFPM present during breakfast service. Employee is only a food handler. The manager is the CFPM, not the normal worker in the breakfast area. A CFPM must be present during all hours of operation. Manager was not present during inspection. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 12/17/2019.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Observed can opener to have accumulation of food debris. Discussed with PIC. COS. Ensure food contact surfaces are washed, rinsed, and sanitized.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.citation_text:
750.540 (C) The food establishment is not under the operational supervision of a Certified Food Service Sanitation Manager that is present at appropriate times. Provide an adequate number of staff with approved training. Reference 750.540.

Observed no CFM during 1st re-inspection. Facility is aware of need for CFM during breakfast hours. Facility is planning on having staff take training class in near future. Paperwork was provided during 2019 inspection.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.citation_text:
750.540 (C) The food establishment is not under the operational supervision of a Certified Food Service Sanitation Manager that is present at appropriate times. Provide an adequate number of staff with approved training. Reference 750.540.

Observed no CFM present at facility during inspection. CFM at facility is on sick leave and the license has expired while on leave. Provided additional paperwork to PIC regarding CFM license training.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114  (P) Quaternary ammonium sanitizer measured 0 ppm at three compartment sink and within sanitization bucket. Maintain concentration at 200 ppm to 400 ppm as indicated on manufacturer's label. Reference 4-501.114.

Observed 0 ppm in both the 3 compartment sink, as well as the sanitization bucket in kitchen. Discussed with PIC that all sanitization with quaternary ammonium must be between 200 and 400 ppm. EcoLab was called during inspection to repair sanitization of 3 compartment sink. COS. 

(REPEAT) 4-501.114  (P) Chlorine sanitizing rinse at dish machine measured at 0 ppm chlorine concentration and 120°F. A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution. Options: 25ppm to 49ppm when the temperature is at least 120°F and the pH is 10 or less; or (2) 50ppm to 99ppm when the temperature is at least 100°F and the pH is 10 or less, or when the temperature is at least 75°F and the pH is 8 or less; or (3) 100ppm when the temperature is at least 55°F and the pH is 10 or less. Reference 4-501.114.

Observed dish machine to have 0 ppm sanitization level of chlorine bleach. EcoLab was called during inspection in order to service dish machine and repair proper sanitization level. Dish machine is in need of new parts and required to be ordered and serviced. Temporary procedure created to utilize dish machine to wash and rinse as the heat level is maintaining correctly, then utilize the quat at 3 compartment sink for at least 90 seconds submerged. Inspector will spot check dish machine on 12/26/2019. This is a repeat violation since last routine inspection.
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(A)  (Pf) Fan within kitchen is not clean to sight and touch. Wash, rinse, sanitize routinely. Reference 4-601.11(A).

Observed fans within kitchen to have large accumulation of dust and debris. Discussed routine cleaning of fans with PIC. COS.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.citation_text:
4-903.11(A) and (C)  (C) Single-Use Articles are stored incorrectly. Single-Use Articles shall be stored: 1) in a clean and dry location; 2) away or protected from contamination; 3) at least six inches above the floor; 4) covered or inverted. Reference 4-903.11(A) and (C).

Observed multiple boxes of single-use utensils (protected within cabinents under service area) to have handles not aligned in same direction in order to hinder cross-contamination when reaching for utensils. Discussed with PIC.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.comment:
Observed the dish machine to be measuring 10ppm. Ecolab came and fixed the dish machine during the inspection.
750-830 All chemical sanitizers in a dish machine must meet the requirements of 21 CFR 178.1010 to ensure all items are properly sanitized.  Rinse water shall not less than 75F. Provide proper sanitizer concentration.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.comment:
Observed a leak at the three compartment sink. Repair the leak.
750-1060 All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code. Repair fixtures in accordance with the Illinois Plumbing Code.

findings.title: Rooms clean, lockers provided and used, clean
findings.comment:
Observed coats stored on clean glassware. Make sure to store personal belongings separate from food.
750-1280 Adequate area must be provided for the storage of employee belongings segregated from the food preparation and food storage area to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Properly store all employee belongings.

findings.title: Approved source
findings.comment:
Observed cooling eggs and sausage under risk type that is not allowed. Facility can cook and discard left over food but cannot cook and cool under medium risk.
750-100 Food shall be obtained from sources that comply with all laws relating to food and food labeling.  The use of home prepared or home canned foods is strictly prohibited.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.comment:
Observed the dish machine not sanitizing properly. Will spot check dish machine, use the three compartment sink until dish machine is fixed.
750-830 All chemical sanitizers in a dish machine must meet the requirements of 21 CFR 178.1010 to ensure all items are properly sanitized.  Rinse water shall not less than 75F. Provide proper sanitizer concentration.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
Observed the handsink needing recaulked to the wall. Make all walls smooth and easily cleanable.
750-1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.

findings.title: No Certified Manager Present
findings.comment:
Observed no IL FSSMC for the site. Facility must have one full time food manager for the risk type.
750-540 All Category II facilities must have at least one full-time Licensed Food Service Sanitation Manager employed at the facility to help ensure proper food handling.  Provide at least one fulltime Food Service Sanitation Manager.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment: Observed plastic containers with burn marks and pitting to be used for hot food prep in a convection oven. Containers were discarded to correct the violation and will be replaced with containers of a durable material that will not melt or pit in a convection oven.750-160  Food shall be protected at all times from cross-contamination.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment: Observed a mixing spatula that has been used to the extent that the food contact surface is no longer smooth and easily cleanable. Food contact surfaces and equipment should be smooth and easily cleanable. Mixing spatula was discarded to correct the violation.750-650a Food contact surfaces shall be smooth, non absorbent, easily cleanable, and free of breaks, open seams, cracks, chips, pits, and free of difficult-to-clean internal corners and crevices.

findings.title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
findings.comment: (1) Observed no chlorine test strips available for testing the sanitizer concentration of the dish machine. Provide chlorine test strips to ensure that dish machine sanitizer is at the appropriate concentration. (2) Observed no thermometer providing for checking cold temperatures for food. Provide a thermometer to ensure that cold temperatures can be checked and monitored. During inspection, thermometer was found and provided to the kitchen staff to check cold holding temperatures. 750-830g A test kit shall be provided and used for checking the concentration of chemical sanitizer that measures the concentration of solution in parts per million.750-830c A thermometer ±3°F shall be provided to check the temperature of  the water in each tank of the dish machine and the temperature of  the final rinse water as it enters the manifold.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment: (1) Observed wet wiping cloth stored on the outside of the sanitizer bucket. Wet wiping cloths shall be stored in the sanitizer solution when not in use. (2) Observed a mixture of soap and san itizer being used in the sanitizer bucket. Do not mix soap and sanitizer. (3) Observed a concentration of 0 ppm quat in the sanitizer bucket on the counter next to the convection oven. Ensure that sanitizer is tested to ensure the appropriate concentration is used.750-810b Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: Observed the following non-food contact surfaces to be soiled: (1) the shelf in the back of the small glass front cooler with food debris and (2) the bottom of the last reach in cooler in the kitchen with food debris. Clean and maintain all non-food contact surface. 750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.comment: (1) Observed dishware including plates and bowls stored for use with the food contact surface exposed. Store dishware with food contact surface protected (inverted). (2) Observed clean silverware stored in dispensers that are heavily soiled with food debris and crumbs at the bottom. Clean and maintain silverware storage containers to prevent contamination. (3) Observed clean knives stored in organizer that are heavily soiled with food debris and dust. Clean and maintain storage containers to prevent contamination and protect clean equipment.750-860 Cleaned and sanitized utensils an equipment shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in a clean, dry location in a way that protects them from contamination by splash, dust and other means.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment: Observed coffee filters stored on the top shelf above the coffee machine uncovered. Single service items such as coffee filters shall always be protected during storage.  Coffee filters should be stored in the plastic or in a clean, lidded container. (2) Observed single service cups stored on the floor underneath the shelving. Single service items shall be protected during storage. Single service items shall be at least six inches off the ground.750-880 Single-service articles shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in closed cartons or containers which protect them from contamination and shall not be placed under exposed sewer lines or  water lines, except for automatic fire protection sprinkler heads may be required by law.750-880 Single-service articles shall be handled and dispensed in a manner which prevents contamination of surfaces which may come in contact with food or with the mouth of the user.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
Observed the hand washing sink in the kitchen to be separating from the wall. Re-seal/re-caulk hand washing sink to wall to provide a smooth, easily cleanable surface.
750-1220 Walls, ceilings, and attached fixtures shall be kept clean. Clean the walls and ceilings.

findings.title: Rooms clean, lockers provided and used, clean
findings.comment: Observed several personal items including a purse and jacket stored on a food storage shelf and in a food storage cabinet. Management states that locker rooms are provided on-site. Cease to store personal articles in food storage or food prep areas. Personal articles shall be stored in designated areas. Use lockers provided.750-1280 Adequate area must be provided for the storage of employee belongings segregated from the food preparation and food storage area to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Properly store all employee belongings.

findings.title: No Certified Manager Present
findings.comment: Facility's current FSSMC has an expired license. Facility is unable to provide proof of a current licensed FSSMC. As a medium risk facility, the facility must have at least one full-time FSSMC employed at the facility. Provide a current licensed FSSMC. Management states that employee has an updated license and will email when available.  750-540 All Category II facilities must have at least one full-time Licensed Food Service Sanitation Manager employed at the facility to help ensure proper food handling.  Provide at least one fulltime Food Service Sanitation Manager.

findings.title: Approved source
findings.comment:
Observed a bag of cooked and cooled sausage patties in the refrigerator. Staff and management was instructed that under their medium risk permit, the facility is not allow to cool or reheat hot foods that have been previously cooked at the facility. Limit hot foods to same day service. Facility voluntarily discarded cooled food to correct the violation.
750-100 Food shall be obtained from sources that comply with all laws relating to food and food labeling.  The use of home prepared or home canned foods is strictly prohibited.

findings.title: Potentially hazardous foods properly thawed
findings.comment:
Observed bags of liquid egg to be improperly thawing in a tub of water. Discussed proper thawing methods with staff and management. Liquid eggs was at 46F and was allowed to be placed back into refrigeration.
750-240 Potentially hazardous foods shall be properly thawed by one of the  following method. 1. Under refrigeration 41°F or below, 2. Under  potable running water 70°F or below or below with sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose food particles into the over-flow, 3. In microwave as part of the cooking process, 4. As part of the cooking process.

findings.title: Potentially hazardous foods properly thawed
findings.comment:
A container of frozen fruit (which included cut melons) was found thawing in hand sink.  Staff had placed it there approximately one hour prior, and fruit was still below 41 degrees F.  It was not under running water.  CORRECTED - manager immediately placed fruit into cooler.  Make sure to thaw frozen foods in one of the four ways listed in IL Food Code (see below, and hand out).

750-240 Potentially hazardous foods shall be properly thawed by one of the  following methods: 
1. Under refrigeration 41°F or below, 
2. Under potable running water 70°F or below or below with sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose food particles into the over-flow, 
3. In microwave as part of the cooking process, 
4. As part of the cooking process.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
Interior ceiling of microwave is soiled with food splash.  Wash, rinse, sanitize, and maintain this surface to minimize potential for cross-contamination amongst microwaving foods.

750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.
750-800d Food-contact surfaces of grills, griddles, and similar cooking devices and the cavities and door seals of microwave ovens shall be cleaned at least once a day.   The food-contact surfaces of all cooking equipment shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other accumulated soil.

findings.title: Hand washing sinks installed, located, accessible
findings.comment:
Upon start of spot-check, large container of frozen fruit was resting in the hand sink, blocking its access for hand washing.  CORRECTED - manager immediately removed fruit and placed it into cooler, freeing up hand sink for hand washing.

750-1120(b) Lavatories shall be accessible to employees at all times.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
(a)  Five packets of cream cheese (stamped "Keep Refrigerated") were found stored on the counter top, as was a can of whipped cream (also marked "Keep Refrigerated").  The cream cheese was at 52 degrees F and the whipped cream was 69 degrees F.  CORRECTED - all five cream cheese packets and the can of whipped cream were immediately, voluntarily, discarded.  Cold-holding, and potentially hazardous foods, was thoroughly discussed.  A new can of whipped cream was brought out and placed into the counter top cooler, which should maintain temperature much better than being set next to the warm waffle irons.

(b) Waffle batter was dispensed and temperature taken with probe thermometer.  Temperature of batter was 62 degrees F.  Kitchen staff stated that batter was made at 8am.  CORRECTED - batter will be used/cooked by customers or discarded by end of breakfast (10am).  Waffle batter must be kept below 41 degrees F after water is added, or TIME must be used as a control (see HACCP topic and IL Food Code handout).

750-120(a) Potentially hazardous foods, shall be maintained at a proper product temperature at all times during storage (41°F or below, or 135°F or above).
750-250  All potentially hazardous foods shall be kept at 41°F or below while on display and service.

findings.title: Thermometers provided and conspicuously placed
findings.comment:
There is not a probe thermometer available by which cold holding temperatures can be measured (current thermometer has a range of 50 - 550 degrees F).  Acquire a thermometer with a range of at least 0 - 220 degrees F so that it can be calibrated with ice water and all cold holding on breakfast bar can be measured.
750-230 A calibratable metal-stemmed thermometer accurate to ±2F° shall be provided for checking temperatures on food.
